title: An optimized protocol for patient-derived xenograft in humanized mice to evaluate the role of IL-34 in immunotherapeutic resistance
protocol: Purchase humanized mice from Jackson Laboratory.
Engraft immunocompromised NSG mice with human hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs).
Intravenously inject 105 CD34+-purified HSCs into 3-week-old female NSG mice, 4 hours after irradiation at 140 cGy.
Determine engraftment levels of human CD45+ cells by flow cytometric quantification in peripheral blood 12 weeks post-HSC transplantation.
Consider mice as engrafted and humanized if over 25% of human CD45+ cells are present in the peripheral blood.
Raise humanized NSG mice in the animal facility after delivery.
Confirm immune cell component of humanized mice from Jackson Laboratory at arrival.
Remove hair from the dorsal flank of the mouse with an electric clipper.
Place mice in the anesthesia chamber.
Prepare a mixture of oxygen/isoflurane with approximately 2% isoflurane in a gas stream.
Prepare 100 mL of serum-free and 1% penicillin/streptomycin RPMI-1640 media.
Thaw the cryopreserved tumor tissues in a heating bath at 37°C for approximately 2 min.
Mix the thawed contents with 10 mL of serum-free RPMI-1640 medium.
Place the tissue in a sterile cell culture dish (10 cm diameter) on ice.
Add 5 mL of 1% penicillin/streptomycin RPMI-1640 medium to keep the tissue moist and prevent it from shrinking.
Mince the tissue into approximately 1 mm³ with a sterile blade.
Anesthetize the humanized mice by isoflurane in the anesthesia chamber.
Pierce ears with ear-punch for identification.
Sterilize the entire shaved area with 70% ethanol.
Insert the trocar needle subcutaneously 1.5 to 2 cm into the mouse flank using a pair of large straight forceps.
Push the plunger of the trocar needle to engraft the tumor fragments and slowly pull out the needle.
Hold the skin with a pair of large straight forceps to ensure the tumor pieces are in proper position, which is 1.5 cm ahead from the insertion point.
Disinfect the skin of the tumor-implanted site with 70% ethanol.
Transfer the mouse to a warm pad and observe until it wakes up from anesthesia.
Measure the size of tumor volume using caliper after 2 weeks of engraftment.
Passage the tumor to another mouse when tumor volume reaches about 500 mm3.
Repeat steps for passaging a tumor from previous measurements.
Engraft the PDX tumor to 14 mice by following specific procedures.
Begin antibody treatment when passaged tumor volumes reach 70–120 mm3.
Intraperitoneally inject 12.5 mg/kg (250 μg) of anti-human IL-34 antibody three times a week for 4 weeks.
Inject combination of anti-IL-34 antibody and anti-PD-1 antibody to the respective groups as per protocol.
Inject 10 mg/kg (approximately 200 μg) of the anti-PD-1 antibody as the first dose and then inject 5 mg/kg every 5 days until endpoint.
Intraperitoneally inject saline twice a week to the control group until study endpoint.
Measure tumor size with caliper twice a week until endpoint.
Collect tumors with resection at day 28 after transplantation.
Prepare samples for histopathological analysis.
Dissect tumor tissues after the endpoint.
Fix dissected tissue samples in a 10% formalin solution for 12 to 24 hours at 22°C–26°C, with a fixation volume five to ten times that of the tissue volume.
Wash the sample once with PBS for 30 minutes.
Soak the sample in 70% ethanol two times at 22°C–26°C for an hour each.
Soak the sample in 90% ethanol one time at 22°C–26°C for an hour.
Soak the sample in 95% ethanol one time at 22°C–26°C for an hour.
Soak the sample in 99% ethanol one time at 22°C–26°C for an hour.
Soak the sample in 100% ethanol three times at 22°C–26°C for an hour each.
Soak the sample into xylene three times at 22°C–26°C for an hour.
Infiltrate the samples with 60°C paraffin four times for an hour.
Embed tissues into paraffin blocks.
Trim the paraffin blocks and cut sections at 4 μm using a microtome and blade.
Place the paraffin ribbon in a water bath at approximately 40°C–45°C.
Mount the sections onto individual slides from the water bath.
Air dry the slides for 30 minutes.
Place the slides in an oven at 45°C–50°C for 8 to 12 hours.
